• Because** energy is lost** as metabolic heat when animals from one trophic level are consumed by species from the next,** energy declines** as it goes up the trophic levels.

• When one creature **eats** another, this happens. 
 
• The **decomposer** organism comes at the end of the chain, having started with the producer **organism. **

questions.question: When a national GST subsumed central taxes on July 1, 2017, how many petroleum goods were kept out of its purview for the time being?

__
 
• **Five petroleum goods** were kept out of the purview of GST for the time being.
 
• The five petroleum goods that were excluded from the GST are **crude oil, natural gas, aviation turbine fuel, diesel, and petrol.**
 
• The reason for keeping these petroleum goods outside the purview of GST is that they generate a significant amount of **revenue** for both the central and state governments, and bringing them under GST would have led to a **substantial loss** in revenue.
 
• The exclusion of petroleum goods from GST has been a subject of debate and criticism, as it leads to **cascading taxes** and** increases the final price** of these goods.
 
• The government has been considering bringing **petroleum goods** under GST, but it has not yet made any concrete decisions in this regard.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **GST** stands for Goods and Services Tax, which is a comprehensive **indirect tax levied** on the supply of **goods and services** in India.
 
• The GST was implemented on **July 1, 2017,** and it replaced multiple indirect taxes that were levied by both the **central and state** governments.
 
• For the purpose of collecting taxes, goods and services are separated into five tax slabs: **0%, 5%, 12%, 18%, and 28%**.
 
• But under the **old tax structure, alcohol, petroleum products, and electricity** were all subject to separate state-level taxes rather than being taxable under the GST.

questions.question:
Parliament consists of _______.

(i) President

(ii) The Council of States

(iii) The House of the People
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Parliament **is the supreme legislative body of India, which consists of the **President **and the two Houses, i.e., the **Council of States **(Rajya Sabha) and the **House of the People** (Lok Sabha).
 
• The President is **not **a member of Parliament but an** integral part** of it as he/she **summons and prorogues **the sessions of Parliament and gives assent to the bills passed by both the Houses.
 
• The **Council of States** (Rajya Sabha) is also known as the Upper House of Parliament, which represents the states and union territories of India.
 
 
• It has a total of **245 members**, out of which 233 are elected by the members of the Legislative Assemblies of the states and union territories, and** 12** are nominated by the President.
 
 
 
• The **House of the People** (Lok Sabha) is also known as the Lower House of Parliament, which represents the people of India.
 
 
• It has a total of **545 members.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 
 

 
• In** New Delhi, **the Parliament convenes at **Sansad Bhavan.**
 
• With **912 million **eligible voters in** 2019**, the Indian Parliament represents the largest **democratic electorate** in the world (the European Parliament comes in second).
 
• A **bill** is the document that **legislative proposals** are presented in front of either chamber of parliament. 
 
• A bill is a draft legislative proposal that becomes an **act of Parliament **after it is approved by both chambers and the president.

• The crops grown in plantation farming are usually cash crops, such as** tea, coffee, rubber, cotton, sugarcane, and palm oil.**
 
• These crops are in high demand and are used for **export** or for domestic consumption.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Some forms of **agroforestry or mixed cropping** may involve growing multiple crops in the same field, which can have** ecological and economic** benefits.
 
• Some plantations may specialize in **two crops** that complement each other, such as **coffee and cocoa,** or sugarcane and ethanol.
 
• Some plantations may adopt **intercropping **or cover cropping techniques to improve **soil fertility **and reduce pest and disease pressure.

questions.question: A batsman scores 50, 56, 42, 38 and 78 in his 5 innings. How much does he need to score in his 6th inning to get his average to 60 in 6 innings?
questions.solution:
**Given**

Scores in first 5 innings = [50, 56, 42, 38, 78]

Target average = 60

**Concept:**

The average is calculated by the total sum divided by the number of elements.

**Calculation:**

⇒ Total score in first 5 innings = Sum of given scores = 50 + 56 + 42 + 38 + 78 = 264

⇒ Target total score for 6 innings = Average × Total innings = 60 × 6 = 360

⇒ Score needed in 6th innings = Target total score - Total score in first 5 innings = 360 - 264 = 96

**Therefore, the batsman needs to score 96 in his 6th innings.**

questions.question: The base diameter of a closed cylinder is 20 cm and its height is 11 cm. Find the total surface area of the cylinder. (Use π = 22/7)
questions.solution:
**Given**

Diameter of the base = 20 cm

Height of the cylinder = 11 cm

π = 22/7

**Concept:** 

The total surface area of a closed cylinder is given by the formula 2πr(h + r), where r is the radius and h is the height of the cylinder.

**Calculation:**

⇒ Radius of the base (r) = Diameter/2 = 20/2 = 10 cm

⇒ Total surface area = 2πr(h + r) = 2 × (22/7) × 10 × (11 + 10) = 1320 cm²

**Therefore, the total surface area of the cylinder is 1320 cm².**

questions.question: 3⁵ + 3⁶ + 3⁷ + 3⁸ is completely divisible by
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Factor out the smallest power of 3 from the expression.

⇒ 3⁵ × (1 + 3¹ + 3² + 3³)

⇒ 3⁵ × (1 + 3 + 9 + 27)

⇒ 3⁵ × 40

Since 40 ends in 0, it is a multiple of 10, making the entire expression perfectly divisible by 10.

**∴ The correct answer is 10.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression = 3⁵ + 3⁶ + 3⁷ + 3⁸

**Calculations:**

⇒ 3⁵ + 3⁶ + 3⁷ + 3⁸

⇒ 3⁵ + (3⁵ × 3¹) + (3⁵ × 3²) + (3⁵ × 3³)

⇒ Taking 3⁵ common from all the terms.

⇒ 3⁵ × (1 + 3 + 9 + 27)

⇒ 3⁵ × 40

⇒ 3⁵ × 4 × 10

⇒ From the simplified step, it is clearly visible that the expression contains 10 as a factor.

⇒ Hence, the given mathematical expression is completely divisible by 10.

**∴ The correct answer is 10.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Factoring Exponential Sums

For sums of consecutive powers of a number, always factor out the smallest power: aⁿ + aⁿ⁺¹ + aⁿ⁺² = aⁿ × (1 + a + a²). The resulting integer bracket factor directly helps identify exact divisibility.

Unit Digit Cyclicity

The unit digit of powers of 3 repeats in a four-step cycle: 3, 9, 7, 1. The sum of any four consecutive powers of 3 will have a unit digit of (3 + 9 + 7 + 1) = 20. Since it ends in 0, it confirms direct divisibility by 10.

Divisibility Rule of 10

A number is divisible by 10 if and only if its last digit is 0. This also means it must simultaneously be divisible by both prime factors 2 and 5.

questions.question: The sides of a triangle are 5 cm, 12 cm and 13 cm. The area (in cm²) of the triangle formed by joining the mid-points of the sides of the triangle is:
questions.solution:
**Given**

Sides of the triangle = [5 cm, 12 cm, 13 cm]

**Concept:**

The triangle formed by joining the mid-points of a triangle is similar to the original triangle and its area is one-fourth of the original triangle.

**Calculation:**

⇒ Area of original triangle (right-angled triangle) = (1)/(2) × base × height = (1)/(2) × 5 × 12 = 30 cm²

⇒ Area of smaller triangle = (1)/(4) × Area of original triangle = (1)/(4) × 30 cm² = 7.5 cm²

**Therefore, the area of the triangle formed by joining the mid-points of the sides of the triangle is 7.5 cm².**

questions.question: The difference between the selling prices of an article available in two schemes of successive discounts 25% followed by 30%, and 25% followed by 20% is Rs. 75. Find the marked price of the article (in Rs.).
questions.solution:
**Given**

Discounts = [25% and 30%, 25% and 20%]

Difference in selling prices = Rs. 75

**Concept:**

Successive discounts can be calculated by taking the product of the reductions, and the difference of the selling prices can be used to calculate the original price.

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let the marked price be x.

⇒ Price after first set of discounts = x × (1 - 25/100) × (1 - 30/100) = x × 0.75 × 0.7

⇒ Price after second set of discounts = x × (1 - 25/100) × (1 - 20/100) = x × 0.75 × 0.8

⇒ Given that the difference between these two is Rs. 75, we have:

⇒ x × 0.75 × 0.8 - x × 0.75 × 0.7 = 75

⇒ x = 75/(0.075) = Rs. 1000

**Therefore, the marked price of the article is Rs. 1000.**

questions.question: R runs for 10 hours at speeds of 10 km/h, 9 km/h,....,1 km/h, respectively, in the first hour, second hour, and so on. His average speed is _______ km/h.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When an object travels at different speeds for equal time intervals, the average speed is simply the arithmetic mean of all the speeds.

Here, the time interval for each given speed is exactly 1 hour.

The speeds form an Arithmetic Progression (AP): 10, 9, 8, ..., 1.

Average Speed = (First Speed + Last Speed) ÷ 2

Average Speed = (10 + 1) ÷ 2 = 11 ÷ 2 = 5.5 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 5.5 km/h.**

**Given:**

⇒ Total time of travel = 10 hours

⇒ Speeds in successive hours = 10 km/h, 9 km/h, 8 km/h, ..., 1 km/h

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

⇒ Distance = Speed × Time

⇒ Sum of first n natural numbers = n(n + 1) ÷ 2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f8a9e3a66c6768169d49c63fbb9df4faeb41e833b8ba9e97ba4d62bd9738ec6d.png]

⇒ Distance covered in 1st hour = 10 km/h × 1 h = 10 km

⇒ Distance covered in 2nd hour = 9 km/h × 1 h = 9 km

⇒ Total Distance covered in 10 hours = 10 + 9 + 8 + ... + 1 km

⇒ Total Distance = (10 × 11) ÷ 2 = 55 km

⇒ Total Time = 10 hours

⇒ Average Speed = 55 km ÷ 10 h = 5.5 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 5.5 km/h.**

Average Speed for Equal Time Intervals

When a person travels at different speeds for exactly the same duration each time, the overall average speed is simply the arithmetic mean of all individual speeds.

Sum of 'n' Natural Numbers

The sum of consecutive natural numbers starting from 1 is computed efficiently using the arithmetic progression formula S = n(n + 1) ÷ 2.

Average Speed for Equal Distances

If equal distances are covered at speeds x and y, the overall average speed is calculated using the harmonic mean formula: 2xy ÷ (x + y).
